newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh police arrest ex-minister over killing.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh police arrest ex-minister over killing.

text.p: Police said on Thursday they had arrested former information minister Taheruddin Thakur for his suspected role in the killing of Bangladesh's independence leader, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, in a 1975 military coup.
Police said Thakur was arrested late on Wednesday at his residence in Dhaka's Nakhalpara area and taken to the Criminal Investigation Department for questioning.

The Sangbad newspaper said the arrest followed a case filed at the city's Lalbagh police station by Muhitul Islam, one of Mujib's private secretaries, who alleged that Thakur was actively involved in the plot to kill Mujib and his family.
Bangladeshi law allows anyone to be detained for up to four months without trial or formal charges.
Three ex-army officers had been arrested in August on charges of killing Mujib, who led Bangladesh to independence from Pakistan in 1971.
The army officers -- retired colonels Farook Reehman and Shahriar Rashid Khan and retired major Mohammad Khairuzzaman -- have been detained in the Dhaka Central Jail.
Bail petitions filed by them have been rejected, police said.

Police were also looking for at least half a dozen other former army officers believed to be involved in Mujib's death and the killing of four top leaders of his Awami League in prison in November 1975.
Thakur was minister under Mujib, whose daughter, Sheikh Hasina, is Bangladesh's current prime minister. Later he joined the government of Mujib's successor, Khandker Mushtaque Ahmed.
